title: Rights and originality boundary
purpose: Separates reusable technique from protected content, lists the asset slots that need new licensed material, and blocks anything that should not be lifted.
boundary: The swarm lifts technique and structure only. Never store, transcribe or reuse the source's footage, frames, music, voice or script text. Keyframes and spectrograms are temporary analysis files in a scratch directory and are never copied into the format IR or a variant. On-screen text may be quoted only as a locating note in evidence.note, at most 6 words, and narration is never quoted. Patterns replace content words with slots, e.g. 'FACT {n}' or '{number} {unit} {noun}'. Analysing a public video for technique is fine; republishing its content is not.
inspect: F1 frames at corners for watermarks and broadcaster marks; F4 sheet for logos, faces and characters; read the other lenses' answers for copied text.
pitfalls: Giving legal conclusions; flag risks and say what needs a human or licence check
Identifying people or tracks by name
Letting a distinctive series name or character into the reusable format

methods.measured: A measurement tool produced the value (an evidence.json field or an ffmpeg/ffprobe filter output). Name the tool and the field.
methods.observed: You looked at extracted frames, crops, scopes, spectrograms or waveforms and saw it. Give the timestamps you looked at.
methods.inferred: Reasoned from measured or observed facts, e.g. 'synthetic voice' from flat pitch on a spectrogram. State the reasoning in the note.
methods.assumed: No direct evidence; a default or convention. Use only for gaps the format needs filled, and keep confidence at 0.3 or lower.

pointer_conventions: ir_path is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the Video format IR (contract schema video_re_format_ir).
A final '/-' means 'append this answer to the array' (the RFC 6901 end-of-array token), e.g. /motion/transitions/- or /generation_rules/-.
A '*' segment means 'each array element the answer is about'; the answer must say which elements (for example beats with role 'item'). The lifter resolves '*' to concrete indexes.
Paths under free-form objects (typography.title, typography.captions, typography.labels, audio.narration, audio.music, render_binding.mapping) use the snake_case key named in the question.

answer_types.enum: exactly one of the question's choices (a string)
answer_types.text: one technique description, at most 300 characters, no copied content
answer_types.list: array of short strings (technique names or kinds)
answer_types.timestamps: array of seconds from the start of the source
answer_types.rule: one procedural generation rule string, at most 400 characters, written in terms of parameters
answer_types.object: a JSON object with the keys the question's how_to_answer names

recipes.F3: Full-resolution crop (add ,scale=iw*2:-1:flags=lanczos to enlarge): ffmpeg -v error -ss T -i "$SRC" -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=W:H:X:Y" "$WORK/crop_T.png"
recipes.F4: Whole-video contact sheet, 1 frame per second: ffmpeg -v error -i "$SRC" -vf "fps=1,scale=180:-2,tile=8x8" -frames:v 1 "$WORK/sheet.jpg" (or use the keyframes and contact sheet from video_re_keyframes_contact_sheet)

questions.question: What exactly may be reused from this video (techniques and structure) and what must not be (footage, frames, music, voice, script text, characters, series identity)?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills source.rights_note, which every downstream step reads.
questions.how_to_answer: Write one note listing reusable technique categories found by the other lenses and the excluded content categories present in this video.
questions.challenge: The note must exclude every content category actually present; check against the contact sheet.

questions.question: Does the video contain third-party footage or images (stock, film or TV clips, news footage, other creators' clips), judging by visible cues?
questions.why_it_matters: Flags content that a variant must replace with its own licensed assets.
questions.how_to_answer: Look for broadcaster bugs, stock watermarks, different creators' overlays, letterboxed film frames on F1 and F3 crops; list timestamps. Method observed or inferred, never a legal conclusion.
questions.challenge: Reject any answer that asserts infringement; it may only flag cues for a human.

questions.question: What must the music slot require in any variant (new original or licensed music, licence field, attribution when the licence needs it, never the source track)?
questions.why_it_matters: Locks the music slot to new licensed or original music regardless of the source.
questions.how_to_answer: Write {source_music_reusable: false, licence_required: true, attribution_when_cc_by: true, cues: [...]} where cues lists observations from music_sfx_mix-030 (lyrics, production cues) without naming any track.
questions.challenge: Any suggestion to reuse, sample or remix the source music is rejected.

questions.question: Is the voice a real, identifiable person's voice that must not be cloned or imitated?
questions.why_it_matters: Locks the voice slot to licensed or synthetic voices that do not imitate the source speaker.
questions.how_to_answer: If narration_voice-002 says human or mixed, set true. Never describe who it is.
questions.challenge: Even if the voice sounds synthetic, cloning or imitating it is not allowed; the answer should still forbid imitation.

questions.question: Are identifiable people shown (faces, names on screen)?
questions.why_it_matters: Flags that people imagery must not be reused and that variants need their own releases or licences.
questions.how_to_answer: Count shots with clearly visible faces or name captions (F4); do not identify anyone.
questions.challenge: Any identification of a person is rejected.

questions.question: Are logos, brand marks or trademarks visible?
questions.why_it_matters: Flags marks that must not appear in variants unless the new content has rights to them.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crops where logos appear; record position and timestamp, not the brand name unless needed to describe the risk.
questions.challenge: Product shots incidental to a fact are still flagged.

questions.question: Does the on-screen text contain distinctive catchphrases or slogans that must not be copied?
questions.why_it_matters: Prevents distinctive phrasing from leaking into templates.
questions.how_to_answer: Review text crops and the pattern answers from other lenses; flag any pattern that preserves distinctive words.
questions.challenge: Check every 'pattern' answer in the swarm output for surviving content words.

questions.question: Are there distinctive characters or mascots whose design is the creator's own?
questions.why_it_matters: Prevents character designs from being copied; the format keeps only the rig type.
questions.how_to_answer: From characters_animation_style answers and F4.
questions.challenge: A generic stick figure is a technique; a named mascot with a recognisable design is not reusable.

questions.question: Are watermarks or creator credits burned into the video?
questions.why_it_matters: Records marks to exclude and helps attribute the analysis.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 corner crops at 3 times.
questions.challenge: Record position and kind only.

questions.question: Which elements together form the source's distinctive identity (series name, signature colour plus layout plus label, recurring character) and should be varied by default in new videos?
questions.why_it_matters: Becomes a rule that variants change at least some identity elements so they are not confusable with the source.
questions.how_to_answer: List combinations of title colour, layout, label pattern and naming that together identify the source; propose which parameter defaults must differ.
questions.challenge: The rule must name parameters, and the IR defaults must actually differ from the source where the rule says so.

questions.question: Which kinds of factual claims in the source must be re-researched (not copied) for a variant?
questions.why_it_matters: Sets claims_need_sources and stops facts being copied without checking.
questions.how_to_answer: From script_rhetoric-029, list claim types; facts in the source are never treated as verified.
questions.challenge: For any factual format, false is rejected.

questions.question: Does the topic involve health, finance, legal or safety advice that needs a higher verification bar?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a verification requirement to the format.
questions.how_to_answer: Classify the topic from captions (analysis only).
questions.challenge: If present even once, it must be listed.

questions.question: Does the video show minors?
questions.why_it_matters: Flags heightened care; minors' images are never reused and variants should avoid depicting identifiable minors without consent.
questions.how_to_answer: F4 contact sheet; count only, no descriptions.
questions.challenge: No descriptions of the people are allowed.

questions.question: Does the video depict dangerous activities that a variant could encourage?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a safety review requirement.
questions.how_to_answer: F4 and captions.
questions.challenge: Give timestamps if true.

questions.question: Will variants built from this format need an AI-content disclosure (synthetic voices, generated people or realistic generated scenes)?
questions.why_it_matters: Adds a disclosure check; platform rules change, so the answer points to the current policy.
questions.how_to_answer: Based on the format's slots (voice, imagery) say which would be synthetic; mark 'check the platform's current policy' rather than stating it.
questions.challenge: Any policy statement without a dated source is rejected.

questions.question: Which IR parameters are asset slots that need a licence field (images, footage, music, voice, fonts)?
questions.why_it_matters: Makes the render step demand licences for every asset.
questions.how_to_answer: Scan the proposed parameters for asset types.
questions.challenge: Every asset parameter must be listed.

questions.question: Do any swarm answers quote more than 6 words of source text or quote narration at all?
questions.why_it_matters: Self-check that the IR stays free of source script text.
questions.how_to_answer: Scan all answer values and notes for quoted strings; count words; report offending answer ids.
questions.challenge: Run the scan again on the merged IR; any hit blocks the lift.

questions.question: Do any answers or IR fields reference source frames, clips or audio files as assets for reuse?
questions.why_it_matters: Ensures keyframes stay analysis-only.
questions.how_to_answer: Scan for file paths or URLs pointing at extracted frames or source media in parameter defaults and source_slot fields.
questions.challenge: Any hit blocks the lift until replaced with an empty asset slot.

questions.question: How was the source obtained (user-supplied file, user's own upload, public URL), and does the user confirm they may analyse it locally?
questions.why_it_matters: Records provenance; the swarm analyses but never republishes.
questions.how_to_answer: Read the run inputs; if unknown, add an open question for the user.
questions.challenge: Do not assume permission; if unknown, keep the open question.

questions.question: Is the source reference (URL or file name and analysis date) recorded?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills source.reference for traceability.
questions.how_to_answer: Copy evidence.source.reference and the run date.
questions.challenge: Must match the evidence bundle exactly.

questions.question: Does the format depend on other people's content (reactions, compilations, duets), so variants would need licensed sources?
questions.why_it_matters: Flags formats that cannot be rebuilt from original or licensed assets alone.
questions.how_to_answer: From shot_list_framing-007 and 002 above.
questions.challenge: Compilation formats must be flagged even if every clip looks freely available.

questions.question: Are there quotes from people shown or read in the video?
questions.why_it_matters: Quotes need their own sourcing in variants and are never copied.
questions.how_to_answer: Captions and text crops with quotation marks or attribution (analysis only).
questions.challenge: Never reproduce the quote.

questions.question: Is sensitive personal information visible (addresses, licence plates, phone numbers, private screens)?
questions.why_it_matters: Prevents carrying such content into notes or the IR.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crops at suspicious frames; report only timestamps and kind.
questions.challenge: The information itself must never be written down.

questions.question: Could numbers or facts in the source be wrong or outdated?
questions.why_it_matters: Reinforces that variants re-research facts.
questions.how_to_answer: Flag claim types with dates or fast-changing values; method inferred.
questions.challenge: This lens does not fact-check; it only flags.

questions.question: What brief should replacement music follow (tempo, instrumentation, mood, length) so it fits without copying?
questions.why_it_matters: Fills the music replacement brief.
questions.how_to_answer: From music lens answers; never name or describe a melody that could be reproduced.
questions.challenge: Reject descriptions specific enough to recreate the source melody.

questions.question: Is the title or caption font likely a commercial font, and what open-licence font class should replace it?
questions.why_it_matters: Prevents unlicensed font use in renders.
questions.how_to_answer: From typography answers; propose an open font class (for example a geometric sans under the SIL Open Font License) and mark the source font as unknown.
questions.challenge: Do not claim to identify the source font.

questions.question: Is there any reason this video should not be lifted at all (hateful, deceptive, harassing, or targeting a private person)?
questions.why_it_matters: A stop gate before lifting.
questions.how_to_answer: Review the contact sheet and captions (analysis only).
questions.challenge: If true, the lift must stop and the reason must be reported.

questions.question: Are there archival or news images with visible rights notices or agency credits?
questions.why_it_matters: Flags images that need licences in variants.
questions.how_to_answer: F3 crops near image edges.
questions.challenge: Record the kind of credit only.

questions.question: Does the parameterised format still contain any source-specific value (exact title text, exact colour plus layout combination, series name) as a default?
questions.why_it_matters: Final check before the format is saved to the library.
questions.how_to_answer: Compare parameter defaults with observed source values flagged in 010.
questions.challenge: Any default equal to a source identity element must change or be justified as generic.

questions.question: Which open questions about rights must a human answer before a variant is published?
questions.why_it_matters: Collects the human review list.
questions.how_to_answer: Gather all open_questions from this lens into a short checklist.
questions.challenge: Every flagged item above must appear.
